title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 64
paragraphs: The Bactrians wore on their heads nearly the same covering as the Medes, and they had native bows of reed and short spears. The Sacae — who are Scythians — wore on their heads caps rising to a point and standing stiff and upright; they wore trousers and carried native bows and daggers, and also axes of the kind called sagaris. These were called the Amyrgian Sacae, though they were in fact Scythians, for the Persians call all Scythians Sacae. The commander of the Bactrians and the Sacae was Hystaspes, son of Darius and of Atossa daughter of Cyrus.
